targetedParagraphRepairs.before: Ask about anxiety and needs and tell the person responsible observations separately from unknowns. Support follows individual assessment and plan. With urgent abnormalities, seek necessary help rather than continuing ordinary questioning.
targetedParagraphRepairs.after: Ask about the person’s anxiety and needs. Tell the person responsible what changes you observed, clearly distinguishing them from what is still unconfirmed. Provide support according to individual assessment and the care plan. If an urgent abnormality occurs, seek the necessary help instead of continuing routine questions.

targetedParagraphRepairs.before: When the person wants to urinate, acknowledge the wish and current condition and support them through an individual method. General capacity values are not holding-time rules or personal diagnoses. Report changes to the person responsible.
targetedParagraphRepairs.after: When the person says they want to urinate, acknowledge their wish and current condition and support them using an individualized method. Do not use general bladder-capacity figures as a reason to make them hold their urine or as a basis for diagnosing disease. Report changes to the person responsible.

targetedParagraphRepairs.before: Consider collection duration, fluid intake, medication, illness and climate with volume. Do not compare 600 mL over half a day as a whole-day amount or invent and double the unmeasured remainder. Check personal baseline and conditions needed for healthcare assessment.
targetedParagraphRepairs.after: Interpret urine volume together with the collection period, fluid intake from food and drinks, medication, illness, climate and other relevant conditions. For example, do not compare 600 mL collected over half a day directly with a full-day reference value, or double it by inventing an unmeasured amount for the rest of the day. Check the person’s usual condition and the circumstances needed for assessment by healthcare professionals.

targetedParagraphRepairs.before: Before changing, check condition, explain purpose and actions and obtain consent. Protect privacy with curtains and prepare supplies, suitable bed height and waterproof protection before starting. Avoid prolonged exposure.
targetedParagraphRepairs.after: Before changing the diaper, check the person’s physical condition, explain the purpose and what you will do, and obtain consent. Protect privacy with curtains or similar measures. Before starting, prepare the necessary supplies, adjust the bed to a suitable working height and prepare a waterproof sheet. Avoid leaving the person’s body exposed for a long time.
